description: Derive account balances from journal entries and compare them with a declared trial balance. Reports an account whose balances differ, with the exact difference; an account carrying a reported balance that nothing in the journal supports; an account with journal movement that appears in no reported figure; and a trial balance whose own debit and credit columns do not foot. Both a debit and credit pair and a single signed balance column are accepted, because exports are written both ways. Pay 220000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

entries.description: Journal entries, each with its lines. Nothing is fetched and no system is connected, so the data supplied is the whole input.

date.description: When the entry is posted. A calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD.

id.description: The posting reference. A repeat is reported, since two postings that cannot be told apart break every reconciliation.

credit.description: The credit, if this line is one. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

debit.description: The debit, if this line is one. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

trial_balance.description: The declared balances. Either a debit and credit pair per account, or a single signed balance.

balance.description: A single signed balance, used instead of the pair when present. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

credit.description: The declared credit balance. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

debit.description: The declared debit balance. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

name: trial_balance_reconciliation

accounts.description: Per account: the journal balance, the declared balance and the exact difference.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

reconciled.description: True only when every account agreed and nothing was left uncompared.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

title: Trial Balance Reconciliation
